persona: Income/dividend investor who lives off yield. Cares about safe high yield (not traps), payout ratio, dividend growth CAGR, no-cut reliability, yield-vs-price-drop, sector income (REITs/utilities/banks/telecom), by country, and yield vs bonds. Wary of yield traps: high yield from a falling price with a cut coming.

cases.question: I need income. Show me the highest-yielding stocks in the world right now.
cases.goal: User wants raw top-yield; a good answer must not just rank on yield but flag trap risk and safety caveats.
acceptance: Surfaces that the very highest yields are often yield traps (high yield driven by a falling price, cut coming)
Does NOT present a pure yield ranking as 'the answer' without a safety/payout-ratio caveat
Suggests pairing yield with payout ratio, price trend, or dividend reliability before acting
Does not give personalized buy advice

cases.question: Find me high but SAFE dividend yields — around 5-7% — where the payout ratio isn't stretched.
cases.goal: Combine yield band with payout-ratio safety; the core safe-high-yield screen.
acceptance: Applies both the yield band and a payout-ratio ceiling (doesn't rank on yield alone)
Explains why payout ratio matters for sustainability (room to keep paying)
Notes payout ratio interpretation differs by sector (e.g. REITs pay out most of cash flow)
Distinguishes safe-looking yields from potential traps

cases.question: Which of these payers are actually growing their dividend, not just paying a fat static one? I want dividend growth.
cases.goal: Screen on dividend growth (CAGR) vs flat/declining payers.
acceptance: Screens/ranks by dividend growth rate, not just current yield
Explains the trade-off: growers often start at a lower yield but compound income
States the reliability window it can actually see (how many years of dividend history it has) rather than implying long-run CAGR it can't verify
Does not fabricate multi-decade growth streaks

cases.question: Give me dividend aristocrats — companies that have raised their dividend every year for 25+ years.
cases.goal: Classic aristocrat request; the assistant likely cannot verify a 25-year streak from its data and must say so.
acceptance: Explicitly states it cannot confirm a 25-year (multi-decade) no-cut/raise streak from the data it has
States the actual history window it can see and offers a best-effort reliability proxy within that window
Does NOT quote or invent a 25+ year streak it cannot verify
Offers the closest honest alternative (e.g. no cut / consistent raise over the years it does have)

cases.question: This telecom is yielding 9% but the stock is down 40% this year. Is this a real income opportunity or a yield trap?
cases.goal: The canonical yield-trap check: high yield born from a price collapse.
acceptance: Recognizes yield rising because price fell is a classic trap signal, not free income
Checks payout ratio / earnings coverage and whether a cut looks likely before endorsing
Looks at why the price dropped (news/fundamentals) rather than treating 9% as attractive on its own
Frames it as trap-vs-safe analysis; avoids a direct buy/sell recommendation

cases.question: อยากได้หุ้นปันผลดีๆ ในกลุ่ม REIT กับสาธารณูปโภค แถวเอเชีย เอาที่ปันผลไม่มีความเสี่ยงจะโดนตัด
cases.goal: Thai: sector income (REITs + utilities) in Asia, wants low cut-risk. Sector + region + safety.
acceptance: Screens REIT and utility sectors within Asia (region + sector filter)
Addresses cut-risk / payout sustainability, not just headline yield
Notes REIT payout ratios naturally run high (distribute most cash flow) so the safety lens differs from ordinary stocks
Can respond appropriately in Thai / to the Thai request
Does not give personalized investment advice

cases.question: Compare dividend income across banks vs utilities vs REITs by country — where do I get the most reliable yield?
cases.goal: Cross-sector, cross-country income comparison with a reliability lens.
acceptance: Compares yield across the three sectors and by country rather than one flat list
Distinguishes headline yield from reliability (payout safety, cut history within its window)
Notes sector-specific payout norms so cross-sector yields aren't compared naively
Caveats the history window for any reliability claim; avoids advice

cases.question: The 10-year US Treasury is around 4.3%. Which dividend stocks give me meaningfully more yield than that but are still safe?
cases.goal: Yield vs bonds: equity income only justified if the extra yield isn't a trap.
acceptance: Uses the bond yield as the hurdle and screens for a meaningful spread above it
Stresses that higher equity yield carries price risk and cut risk that bonds don't — extra yield must be safe, not just higher
Applies a payout/safety filter, not yield alone
Does not recommend a specific allocation or give personalized advice

cases.question: Is XYZ's dividend safe? I hold it for income and I'm worried they might cut.
cases.goal: Single-name payout-safety check — the assistant must assess coverage without predicting the future.
acceptance: Examines payout ratio / earnings coverage and dividend history it can see, not just the current yield
Checks recent news / fundamentals for cut-risk signals
Is honest that it cannot predict a future cut, only assess current safety indicators
States the history window and avoids claiming a streak it can't verify; no buy/hold/sell advice

cases.question: หาหุ้นปันผลที่จ่ายมาตลอดไม่เคยตัดปันผลเลยหลายปี แล้วก็ค่อยๆ เพิ่มปันผลขึ้นทุกปีด้วย
cases.goal: Thai: wants no-cut reliability + steady dividend growth (aristocrat-style, honest window).
acceptance: Screens for consistent no-cut record AND rising dividends together
States clearly how many years of dividend history it actually has (reliability window) instead of implying 'always / forever'
Does not fabricate an unbroken multi-year/multi-decade streak beyond its data
Can respond in Thai; distinguishes reliable growers from static high-yielders and avoids advice
